sub_branches.concept: Perpendicular Bisector, Angle Bisector & Angle Copying
details: Straightedge & compass are the sole classical instruments permitted.
Perpendicular Bisector: Draw intersecting arcs from endpoints X, Y with radius > 0.5 XY. Proved via SSS triangle congruence.
Equidistance Property: Any point on perpendicular bisector is equidistant from segment endpoints.
Angle Bisector & Copying: Bisecting angles by intersecting arcs; copying angles by recreating congruent triangle using SSS.
evidence_or_examples: Bisecting segment XY to construct symmetrical eye design
Constructing parallel line by copying alternate interior angle

details: 60° Angle: Arc radius unchanged from vertex forms equilateral triangle.
Regular Hexagon: 6 equilateral triangles meeting at center (6 × 60° = 360°). Constructed by stepping off radius 6 times around circle. Interior angle = 120°.
evidence_or_examples: Constructing a regular hexagon of side 4 cm on a circle
Designing pointed arches and 6-pointed star rosettes

details: Tiling (Tessellation): Covering a 2D plane with repeating shapes with strictly ZERO gaps and ZERO overlaps.
Tangram: Ancient Chinese 7-piece puzzle dissecting a square into 5 triangles (2 large, 1 medium, 2 small), 1 square, 1 parallelogram.
evidence_or_examples: Arranging 7 Tangram pieces to form arrow, animal, and human silhouettes
